title: Getting the Words Right -- Plans, Decisions and Commitments
desc: Verbs followed by -ing or by to, for the decisions, suggestions and promises that come out of every meeting. Key expressions: to arrange, to afford, to refuse, to admit, to tend to, to involve, to put off, to manage to, to give it a shot, to go through the motions, to be worth, to look forward to. Structure: suggest doing, decide to do, and remember to or remember doing.
vocab: To arrange
to organize the details of something so that it can happen
I will arrange a call with the Santiago team for Thursday.
To afford
to have enough money or time to do something
We cannot afford to lose another corporate account this year.
To refuse
to say clearly that you will not do something
The director refused to sign the proposal as it was.
To admit
to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true
Julio admitted forgetting to send the Lima figures.
To tend to
to usually do something, or to be likely to do it
Clients tend to book late when prices are going up.
To involve
to include something as a necessary part
The new role involves traveling to Lima every month.
To put off
to delay something until a later time
We cannot put off the decision until next quarter.
To manage to
to succeed in doing something difficult
We managed to close the deal before the convention.
To give it a shot
to try something, even if you are not sure it will work
The new format might not work, but let us give it a shot.
To go through the motions
to do something without real interest or effort
Nobody believed in the plan, so we just went through the motions.
To be worth
useful or important enough to justify the time or effort
It is worth calling the client before you send the email.
To look forward to
to feel happy about something that is going to happen
I look forward to meeting the new team in Buenos Aires.

paras: On Monday the commercial team met to plan the next six months in South America. It was a long meeting, and it ended with three decisions that Rosa now has to put into an email for the regional director.

First, the team decided to postpone the regional meeting until September, because they could not afford to fly twelve people to Lima before the new fares were approved. Nobody enjoyed making that decision, but everybody agreed to accept it.

Second, the director suggested reviewing the whole proposal before submitting it again. He refused to sign the current version, and he recommended asking the legal team for help with the contract terms.

Third, Julio admitted forgetting to send the Lima figures. He remembered sending the draft, but not the numbers. Rosa did not make it a problem. She arranged to call the two clients in Santiago on Thursday and asked Julio to stop worrying and send the figures that afternoon.

context_quiz: 1. Why did the team decide to postpone the regional meeting?
Because the director preferred to hold it in Santiago instead of Lima, closer to the clients.
Because they could not afford to fly twelve people to Lima before the new fares were approved.
Signing the current version of the proposal as soon as the legal team approved it.
Reviewing the whole proposal before submitting it again.
3. What does "Julio remembered sending the draft" mean?
He has a memory of sending the draft.
He did not forget that he still had to send the draft to the director before Thursday.
4. What did Rosa ask Julio to do?
To call the two clients in Santiago himself on Thursday, and to apologize for the delay.
To stop worrying and send the figures that afternoon.
To write the email to the director.

tip.title: Verbs Followed by -ing or to
tip.intro: Some verbs are followed by -ing, some by to + base verb, and a few take both with a different meaning. There is no perfect rule, so learn the ones you use at work.
rows: enjoy, avoid, consider, suggest, recommend, finish, keep, admit, mind, risk, involve
want, need, decide, plan, hope, expect, agree, refuse, offer, manage, afford, tend, arrange, fail
With to: the action you do next. With -ing: the action itself, or a memory.
Always -ing, including the to of look forward to.
"We decided not to sign." · "I regret not calling earlier."
tip.outro: The verb that most often goes wrong in business emails is suggest: it never takes to. Say I suggest reviewing it or I suggest that we review it.

blanks: Hint: suggest is followed by the -ing form
She suggested reviewing the proposal again.
Hint: decide is followed by to plus the base verb
We decided to postpone the regional meeting.
Hint: the to in look forward to is a preposition, so use -ing
I look forward to hearing from you.
Hint: afford is followed by to plus the base verb
We cannot afford to lose this account.
Hint: admit is followed by the -ing form
Hint: a task you must not forget takes to
Please remember to copy the director.

order.intro: Listen to the summary of the conversation, then put the steps in the correct order.
items: Julio tells Rosa that the director decided to postpone the regional meeting until the third quarter.
Rosa says she is not surprised, because Santiago kept asking for more time.
Julio explains that the director suggested reviewing the whole proposal and refused to sign it as it was.
Julio admits forgetting to send the Lima figures, although he remembers sending the draft.
Rosa decides to arrange a call with Santiago for Thursday and asks Julio to give the new format a shot.

speech: We decided to postpone the meeting until September.
I suggest reviewing the proposal before we send it.
We cannot afford to lose this account.
I admit forgetting to send the figures.
I look forward to hearing from you.

quiz.intro: You are writing to clients and colleagues after a planning meeting. Choose the best sentence.
items: 1. You want to propose a review of the contract. You write:
I suggest to review the contract with the legal team before we send it to the client.
I suggest reviewing the contract.
I suggest review the contract.
2. You end an email to a new client. You write:
I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward to hear from you and to working with your whole team next quarter.
I look forward hear from you.
3. You explain why you said no to a discount. You write:
We cannot afford losing more margin on this route, so the discount is not possible this year.
We cannot afford lose more margin.
We cannot afford to lose more margin.
4. A colleague forgot to send a file. He tells the director:
I admit to forget the file, but I will send it to you and to the legal team before the end of the day.
I admit forgetting the file.
I admit forget the file.
5. You are not sure a new idea will work, but you want to test it. You say:
Let us give it a shot.
Let us go through the motions and present the idea to the director anyway, even if nobody believes in it.
Let us put it off.

think: Imagine you are presenting My Plan for the South American Expansion to your director. Record about ninety seconds. Say what you want to do, what you would avoid doing, what the team has already managed to do, and what you are looking forward to. Use at least six verbs from this lesson: three followed by -ing and three followed by to.
survival: We decided to postpone the meeting until September.
I suggest reviewing the proposal before we send it.
We cannot afford to lose this account.
I admit forgetting to send the figures.
I look forward to hearing from you.
